articles.title: First Plot Details for Zack Snyder’s Escape from New York Remake
articles.summary: The 300 and Man of Steel director discussed the setting for his Escape from New York remake and revealed he may also already have someone lined up to star as Snake Plissken.
articles.body:
Director Zack Snyder has discussed the first plot details for his upcoming Escape from New York remake, revealing when the movie will be set and the fact that he may already have someone lined up to star as Snake Plissken. Snyder’s comments came via a conversation with Happy Sad Confused host Josh Horowitz at the Toronto International Film Festival, where Snyder is showcasing his new film The Last Photograph.

“The approach is… the movie’s going to be set in ’97… from the perspective of 1981,” said Snyder. “The war between the United States police force and… the criminal elements takes place, I think, July 9th, 1981 – which is the release date of the original movie. And then the rest is pretty much Escape from New York.”

After explaining his love of the original film, which is also set in 1997 and he regards as “the perfect combination of kitsch and camp,” Snyder was pressed whether he already has his Snake Plissken.

Snyder would not be drawn on whether it’s an actor he’s worked with previously, but he did confirm Watchmen and Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice actor Jeffrey Dean Morgan’s claims he’s been badgering Snyder for a role in the project.

“He literally has been hitting me up,” said Snyder, joking he doesn’t need to send him an audition tape. “No, he’s the best; I love him.”

The original Escape from New York, directed by filmmaking icon John Carpenter (who also co-wrote the script and worked on the score), stars Kurt Russell as Snake, an ex-special forces soldier forced into a 24-hour mission to rescue the President of the United States. Snake must infiltrate Manhattan, which has been converted into a sprawling maximum security prison, and get out again before the explosives implanted into his body go off.

The film was a critical and commercial hit, and has carved out a well-deserved reputation as an influential sci-fi cult classic. A remake of the film has been bouncing around for over two decades, but appears now to be finally gathering momentum, with StudioCanal indicating it was moving full speed ahead on the project in April this year.

Whoever steps up to be Snake, just don’t expect Kurt Russell’s son to be the one taking on the role , with Wyatt Russell ruling that out back in 2021.

“If I really wanted to get people sending me hate mail, I think that’s what I should do,” said the Thunderbolts* star. “I will not be ever doing anything like that.”

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

articles.title: Professor Layton Developer Level-5 Scrambles to Reupload Trailers as AI Backlash Intensifies
articles.summary: In the wake of fierce online backlash, Professor Layton developer Level-5 has released a new statement apologizing for the mistrust caused by generative AI use in its recent showcase for upcoming titles, insisting some examples spotted by fans were simply human error.
articles.body:
In the wake of fierce online backlash, Professor Layton developer Level-5 has released a new statement apologizing for the mistrust caused by generative AI use in its recent showcase for upcoming titles, insisting some examples spotted by fans were simply human error.

Not only that, but the studio has insisted that some mistakes flagged as AI errors by eagle-eyed commenters on social media were actually human mistakes. The Japanese studio has now vowed to clean up these offending portions.

For those who missed it, Level-5 released its “VISION 2026 II: Dreams” presentation on YouTube on September 10. Narrated by a cartoon version of CEO Akihiro Hino, the showcase walked viewers through the studio’s upcoming releases, including Yokai Watch 2: Haunted Domain, Decapolice, and a first look at Professor Layton and the New World of Steam .

However, shortly after the video dropped, social media was flooded with comments and reaction videos . Commenters scrutinized backgrounds and art, noting inconsistencies and elements suggestive of generative AI use, with many slamming Level-5 for perceived “AI slop.” Comparisons between the September 9 Nintendo Direct Yokai Watch 2 trailer and the VISION 2026 trailer for the same game released just a day later also had fans pointing out AI-like errors. The Nintendo Direct trailer for Professor Layton and the Curious Village (a Switch remake of the Nintendo DS original), also had internet sleuths finding elements that appeared to be AI upscales of original backgrounds.

Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03 — AmericanYoshi (@AmericanYoshi) September 10, 2026

Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03

This backlash prompted CEO Hino to make a statement on X , admitting that the developer had experimented with using AI processing techniques for the VISION 2026 II showcase out of a “desire to make the presentation flashy." After apologizing for the offense that this caused, Hino insisted that key elements of Level-5's games (such as story, character designs and settings) were created by people and that AI tools were used to speed up the process of digitizing artists’ creations. “Please be reassured that there is no simplistic, AI-generated data in our released games,” Hino commented, before noting that the company’s use of AI tools to make processes more efficient was giving its developers more time to be creative, and that they are currently in a trail-and-error process of shortening the 5-year development cycle for major titles down to two years.

Hino’s statement went down like a lead balloon, however. The CEO’s comments about “using AI in various ways” to enhance the visual appearance of the showcase drew particular ire, with many Japanese users seeing this as a lazy ‘style over substance’ approach. “Isn’t the point of a trailer to express creativity, not flashiness?” one person said.

Many commenters in both Japanese and English also pointed out the ethical issues with how generative AI has been trained on copyrighted works of artists, and how Level-5’s attitude towards gen AI creates distrust among fans. “I think human spirit is more important than the speed of game releases, so wouldn’t it be better to not use AI, even if it takes five years? Even if just one asset is AI-generated, people will never stop worrying about whether a song, image or line of dialogue is AI or human-made. Isn’t maintaining trust the most important thing?” another commenter responded in Japanese. As a side note, Level-5’s concept image for its TGS booth also got flagged as a suspected AI image, prompting further angry comments.

Professor Layton and the New World of Steam Level 5 Vision Trailer Stills

In its latest statement issued on September 17, Level-5 said: “We deeply apologize for the distrust in our production process that our inexperienced use of AI and simple human errors have caused. Please note that AI has not been used directly in the contents of the games themselves. Moving forward, we will pay even greater attention to the accuracy and quality of the work we produce.”

Level-5 also said that it will clean up “errors caused by AI use, as well as human mistakes that look like AI errors,” and upload corrected versions of the trailers to coincide with Tokyo Game Show, which opens to the public this weekend. At the time of writing, Level-5 has uploaded TGS versions of trailers for Decapolice and Holy Horror Mansion to its official YouTube channel .

In its September 17 statement, Level-5 published a side-by-side of Yokai Watch 2’s promotional illustration before and after mistakes had been edited out. Addressing comments made by users regarding the telephone lines looking “unnatural,” the company stated that its artist had used a real photo of telephone lines they had taken themselves as a reference, and intentionally simplified the lines to fit the background, which resulted in this “being misconstrued as AI.” “These telephone lines were actually hand-drawn by our in-house designer, however, to prevent any further misunderstandings, we have corrected them so that they look more natural,” Level-5 said.

But what about other details flagged by commenters as possible signs of gen AI usage? Level-5 said that, “Similarly, other issues that people pointed out, such as with the vending machine and guttering, were also the result of human error in omitting these details. The brake levers on the bicycle were not drawn in past Yokai Watch 2 games. However, we feel they should have been drawn for this latest game, considering the higher level of detail.”

⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭 #YOKAIWATCH Hier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7 — Yo-net Watch (@YonetWatch) September 10, 2026

⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭 #YOKAIWATCH Hier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7

Many commenters also picked up on how Kenta/Nathan’s face looks different in the Level-5’s VISION 2026 II showcase and the Nintendo Direct that was released on the previous day. In response, Level-5 said, “We did not make any alterations or corrections using AI.” It said it was unable to correct Nathan’s low-poly appearance in time for Nintendo Direct’s submission deadline but had updated the model by the time of its own showcase, which explains why Nathan looks different in trailers that were made public just one day apart. Level-5 also stated that “no AI was used in Professor Layton and the New World of Steam,” however it did not comment on whether or not AI was used for the Curious Village remake.

Level-5 wrapped up its statement by apologizing again for the distrust caused by its “inexperienced use of AI and human error," promising to take more care in the future to avoid such mistakes. “From now on, we will limit our AI usage to enhancing efficiency, and will avoid directly using it in videos released directly to our fans.”

This statement also did not go down well. “I don’t think they understand WHY using AI is bad. We weren’t mad at the little errors that AI produced, we just used those errors to determine if it was AI or not, because using AI at all is bad. Now they are going to continue using AI but they are going to hide it better,” one commenter responded .

It's not about reducing the use of AI, but about eliminating it entirely. pic.twitter.com/ziJuMrxBsm — Turo (@Any_Turo) September 16, 2026

It's not about reducing the use of AI, but about eliminating it entirely. pic.twitter.com/ziJuMrxBsm

Many Japanese comments also criticized the Level-5 statement for blaming human error. “You promised not to use gen AI going forward, but aren’t you just shifting the blame onto the staff?” replied one commenter. “I think the main reason for all this criticism is President Hino’s stance of repeatedly promoting generative AI usage without confronting its fundamental issues (such as unauthorized use of data and environmental pollution).”

Level-5 has been experimenting with gen AI tools to speed up game development and improve efficiency for at least the last three years. Back in December 2023, the studio released an extensive presentation on its use of AI tools to a Japanese government study group (source: Automaton /ITMedia). In short, it has been using Stable Diffusion to generate layout ideas for promotions, and to create 3D versions of the original 2D models from older games, like its Yokai Watch series. However, the company pointed out then that these generative AI outputs were just used as guidelines for its human artists, who produced the final output. In the same presentation, it described combining parts of AI-generated images with creations by its artists to make the in-game backgrounds (including stadium crowds and buildings) for soccer RPG Inazuma Eleven: Victory Road.

However, it remains to be seen how much the studio’s attitude towards AI usage costs it in terms of players’ trust in the company.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

articles.title: Will Scarlet Witch Appear in Vision Quest? Paul Bettany Says It's a 'Matter of Secrecy,' and Fans Are Now Hoping For Her Return
articles.summary: Paul Bettany has claimed he still doesn't know if Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch will return in Vision Quest, but fans have hope.
articles.body:
Paul Bettany has claimed he still doesn't know if Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch will return in VisionQuest .

The promising-looking Disney+ show is set to conclude the trilogy of series that began with WandaVision, and fan hopes are high that some kind of cameo from Wanda Maximoff will take place.

Audiences last saw Wanda during the finale of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, as she brought down Mount Wundagore and was seemingly buried underneath a mountain of stone. But... we didn't see a body, and all comic book fans should know what that means!

Asked whether his on-screen partner would finally return in VisionQuest, Bettany told Entertainment Today that the answer to this was a secret that even he didn't know the answer to, sparking fan speculation that an appearance by Olsen may have been filmed.

"That is, at this point, a matter of secrecy," Bettany claimed. "And it's secret even to me. There are also other surprises to come, and other big reveals. It's very exciting, I think, the story is really compelling and interesting."

While VisionQuest is not directly about Wanda, fans still want to see Scarlet Witch return in some form. An appearance would help round out the WandaVision trilogy that began by focusing on her relationship with the re-animated synthezoid and continued by revealing that the couple's imaginary kids were now real. (It's complicated.)

Agatha All Along featured Heartstopper star Joe Locke as Billy Maximoff, while VisionQuest is set to introduce Ruaridh Mollica as Tommy Maximoff. Surely Marvel is building to a full family reunion, with Wanda included?

More pressing, though, is the expectation that Wanda will join the vast group of fan-favorite Marvel characters to appear in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday and next year's Avengers: Secret Wars. Could a cameo for VisionQuest have been filmed recently? Avengers: Doomsday reshoots did recently take place — so perhaps Bettany really doesn't know yet if something has been added in post-production. Or, of course, he absolutely does know if Wanda is in the show (or not) and is simply keeping the truth hidden.

"I suspect the post credit scene will be Wanda alive and working for Doom," one fan speculated. "I think it’ll be from the recent Doomsday reshoots we know Elizabeth Olsen attended." (This references recent, unverified internet speculation prompted by a potential sighting of Olsen flying into the U.K. around the time Doomsday reshoots took place.)

"Especially since this show has repeatedly been referred to as the third in the Wanda-Vision family trilogy," a second fan replied. "If this is the end of a trilogy that began with her alone and manifesting a family which is then broken, scattered and reborn, it makes narrative sense for them to come together again at the close."

"Rule #1 no body, no death," said a third.

VisionQuest begins streaming on October 18 via Disney+, so there's not long until we find out.

articles.title: How Turok: Origins Hopes to Appeal to a New Generation 30 Years After the Original N64 Game
articles.summary: There is a generation of gamers who know Turok well. For me, it is first and foremost an N64 game, a dinosaur-killing first-person shooter alternative to Rare’s all-conquering GoldenEye. But there is a generation of gamers who have never even heard of Turok before, let alone played it. So how does developer Saber get younger gamers interested in playing the upcoming Turok: Origins?
articles.body:
There is a generation of gamers who know Turok well. For me, it is first and foremost an N64 game, a dinosaur-killing first-person shooter alternative to Rare’s all-conquering GoldenEye. But there is a generation of gamers who have never even heard of Turok before, let alone played it. So how does developer Saber get younger gamers interested in playing the upcoming Turok: Origins ?

The answer, Saber development chief Tim Willits told me at gamescom 2026, is co-op. Playing with friends is massively important for younger gamers, he said, and so Saber has made sure to include it as a feature.

“It's been a balancing act to make sure that we had enough elements in it to make guys like you happy, like the Cerebral [Bore] gun, some throwbacks to the original Turok player, some other elements,” Willits said. "You can play first-person or third-person. So we want guys like you to be like, ‘Oh, this is cool.’ And then the dinosaur bosses are awesome.

“But we also want to make sure that we can get fans who have never played a Turok game. Like my kids, they're 22, they have never even heard of Turok. So we want to also build a game that looks amazing, plays great. You can play it by yourself or with one friend or two friends. We want to appeal to new players that have never played a Turok game as well.

“That's been our guiding principle with Turok. Add things that people like you would appreciate and like, but build a game that could be attractive to new players.”

You can see this theory in action across the video game industry. While single-player games remain enormously popular, hangout games have generated and continue to generate billions of dollars. Battle royales such as PUBG and Fortnite were built on the back of groups of friends chatting while playing. COVID lockdowns only accelerated the need for video games as social spaces, with Call of Duty battle royale Warzone an early beneficiary. Extraction shooters such as Escape from Tarkov and, more recently, Arc Raiders, were also fueled by friends who played together. A lot of the appeal of Helldivers 2 came from the shenanigans you could get up to with your friends.

Then there’s the rise of ‘friendslop’ games, which are massive across Steam (Roblox clones are incredibly popular, too). And we have a perfect example of this appeal only recently: Bulkhead’s hit Steam game Wardogs is a shooter that revolves around playing with friends. “I truly believe it is not about the mode, it’s about letting players run wild,” Bulkhead boss Joe Brammer recently tweeted . “The more you constrain players the less fun it is, FPS games are social experiences and Wardogs is closer to Mecca Chameleon than COD.”

Enter Turok: Origins, which shouldn’t be compared to something like Wardogs or a battle royale, of course, but it does let teams of three players join up to shoot dinosaurs in the face. Think Space Marine 2 but instead of fighting Tyranids, you’re fighting dinosaurs with lasers.

“It looks amazing,” Willits continued. “The big giant boss fights — I'm not even sure if this is a term — do you know the boss run games? It has that kind of feel to it. And wait till you see some of our cool bosses! And then playing with the friends, it's really important to young gamers now. Like you and I are like, we play by ourselves. We're old. So you can play either way, but it's really important to a huge audience to at least have the option to play with someone else.

“Because young people use video games as a social connection more so than you and I did, because we grew up in different times. And so it looks great, play is fun. The Echoes [you collect Echoes to unlock Turok powers] are amazing. The boss runs are sweet and you can play with your friends. So I feel it has those elements that will attract new people.”

Turok: Origins is due out spring 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and Nintendo Switch 2. Check out our Turok: Origins hands-on preview for more.

articles.title: Pokémon TCG 30th Anniversary ETB Price Drops on Amazon, but There Is Still a Catch
articles.summary: Amazon US is accepting invite requests for Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration ETBs at $84—roughly $96 below market resale value on TCGplayer.
articles.body:
The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration set is finally here , and if you've been trying to pick up some of its more desirable products without paying a hefty premium, things aren't exactly getting easier. The set has been difficult to find at sensible prices since launch, making Amazon's latest price drop on the 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box particularly interesting.

Amazon currently has the 30th Celebration ETB listed for just $83.44 , down from the $89.99 price we spotted previously. That's still above the set's MSRP, but it's a considerably more appealing price than some of the inflated listings we've seen elsewhere.

There's one rather important catch, though. Amazon still hasn't sent out its invite emails , so requesting an invite doesn't guarantee you'll actually get the chance to buy one at $83.44.

The timing here is worth paying attention to. When we first spotted Amazon taking invite requests, the 30th Celebration set hadn't yet fully hit the market. Now that the 30th Anniversary collection is officially out, we're seeing just how difficult some of its products can be to find at a reasonable price .

That's especially true for the more desirable sealed products, with the 30th Celebration ETB becoming increasingly difficult to track down without paying above MSRP. Amazon's $83.44 listing therefore stands out, even if it isn't the kind of below-MSRP bargain we normally hope to find.

The bigger problem is that requesting an invite doesn't mean Amazon will actually offer you the ETB . The retailer previously introduced invite requests for this product in the US, an unusual move given that Amazon's US Pokémon TCG listings have traditionally been priced much closer to prevailing market prices.

If Amazon does eventually send you an invite, you'll then have to decide whether $83.44 is a price you're comfortable paying for the ETB.

That's a slightly different proposition now that the 30th Anniversary set is actually on sale and sealed products are proving harder to find. You're not getting it at MSRP, but you may be avoiding the considerably more painful prices being asked by resellers.

And that's really the awkward part of buying Pokémon TCG products right now. MSRP is still the number I'd ideally want to see, but when a popular set is difficult to find, the choice can quickly become paying a premium to a major retailer or paying an even larger premium on the secondary market.

For now, $83.44 at Amazon is one of the more interesting prices to keep an eye on, assuming Amazon actually starts sending those invites.

articles.title: New GTA 5 Leak Suggests Rockstar Had Ambitious, City-Sized DLC Plans That Were Ultimately Scrapped
articles.summary: GTA 5 has suffered a new leak that suggests Rockstar Games had ambitious, city-sized DLC plans for the game.
articles.body:
GTA 5 has suffered a new leak that suggests Rockstar Games had ambitious, city-sized DLC plans for the game.

Reports emerging online today indicate a near 200GB version of the GTA 5 source code initially leaked in 2023 has now been made public, and interested parties are analyzing it as we speak. The highlight here is what looks like a Liberty City DLC for GTA 5 that obviously never saw the light of day (GTA Online’s enormous success steered Rockstar away from story DLC towards multiplayer focused updates).

According to X / Twitter user TJGM , the Liberty City DLC found in the files has been extrapolated and visualized to show just how much bigger this version of the city is compared to the one found in GTA 4. “Here's a look at the expanded Liberty City layout,” they tweeted. “This outline of the map is drawn based on where shorelines are, the lines indicate zones that play shoreline audio.”

There is speculation online that this Liberty City DLC may have been held back for GTA 6, but there is no evidence to suggest that is Rockstar’s plan.

More has emerged from this leak: Agent Trevor DLC mission names; cut vehicles, cut dialogue, cut cutscenes, and more.

On Agent Trevor, GTA fans have known for some time that Rockstar worked on a single-player DLC for GTA 5 that would have seen Trevor assume the role of a secret agent. In 2024, actor Steven Ogg said Rockstar originally planned to make a story expansion focused on his character, Trevor , with it thought to have fallen by the wayside as the developer focused on the cash cow that was GTA Online.

Ogg was joined by Michael actor Ned Luke and Franklin actor Shawn Fonteno in a Questions and Answers session with Streamily , and the trio shed light on what they claimed was scrapped downloadable content for GTA 5 that starred Trevor as a Federal Investigation Bureau agent.

"Originally they were gonna do continuing stories of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor," Luke said, and Ogg expanded on his version. "We also had that really cool s**t of — and I forget if it was DLC, I have no idea — but where Trevor was gonna be undercover, he works for the FEDs," Ogg said. "And we did shoot some of that stuff with James Bond Trevor. He's still kind of a f**k up but he's doing his best. And we shot some stuff and then it just disappeared and they never followed up on it."

Also in 2024, Joe Robino, who was a senior camera artist and virtual cinematographer working at Rockstar’s New York office from 2010 to 2016, spoke to the SanInPlay YouTube channel about why the GTA 5 story DLC was canceled .

“A lot of the team went to do Red Dead Redemption 2 right away and I took on this other project that was a standalone DLC for GTA that never came out and it was kick ass,” Robino revealed.

“That was my thing. I was one of the main editors, camera artists, and on-stage stuff. We split our teams into two. I stayed on GTA Online and then this DLC, which Steven Ogg [the actor who played Trevor Philips] was a very important part of.

“And then some of the team overlapped and went to RDR2 early on, and then we just kind of did this [flipped motion], because when that game got shelved, we spent so much money… a lot of that stuff though did end up making it I believe into later iterations of GTA Online, I think. So it’s not like they wasted it.

“It was really really good. But when GTA Online came out it was so much of a cash cow and people were loving it so much that it was hard to make an argument that a standalone DLC would outcompete that. I think looking back now you could probably do both. But that was a business decision they made. I was a little upset about that.

“That actually was a lot of the reason for me being a little sour at that time. Because I was like yo, WTF guys? This s**t’s awesome. Let’s keep going. Let’s finish this s**t.”

Fans have had snippets of information about GTA 5’s fabled story DLC over the years. GTA dataminers have also discovered a reference to Trevor with a jetpack , which suggests story mode DLC was repurposed into GTA Online, as Robino said. In 2018, Rockstar finally unveiled GTA Online's Doomsday Heist missions alongside the Thruster jetpack.

Last year, speaking on the Lex Fridman podcast , Rockstar Games co-founder and former lead writer Dan Houser addressed the DLC for the first time, insisting that if the developer had continued with it, it wouldn’t have been able to make 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2 .

“The internet knows we made a DLC… single-player DLC for GTA 5 that never came out,” Houser said.

“It was one when you played as Trevor, but he was a secret agent. It was cute. It never quite came together, and it was never finished. It was about half done when it got abandoned. But I think if that had come out, we probably wouldn’t have gotten to make Red Dead 2. So, there are always compromises.”

What approach will Rockstar take with GTA 6 ? Will it go back to story DLC, or focus on whatever new version of GTA Online it has up its sleeve? Some think Rockstar will eventually add multiple cities, including Liberty City, to GTA 6, alongside GTA Online 2 or whatever the multiplayer mode ends up being called. For now, though, it’s a case of what might have been for GTA 5.

Last week, as part of the ongoing employment tribunal to determine the fate of the 31 GTA 6 developers Rockstar fired last year, the company revealed the extreme lengths it goes to in order to prevent security breaches .

Rockstar has suffered a string of high-profile leaks over the years, most recently the 'CyberLeek' incident which saw GTA 6 gameplay hit the internet ahead of the game's Netflix special. Speaking at the tribunal, Rockstar said it's under intense scrutiny as the developer of GTA.

“Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula,” Rockstar said, adding that it adopts “the security posture of a Wall Street bank.”

In April 2025, Rockstar dismissed an employee in Lincoln, UK, who it alleged disclosed confidential information about GTA 6 to a third party who then published the information to social media. Rockstar dismissed an employee in the U.S. in November 2023 and another in India in November 2025 for two separate acts of information leaking.

Rockstar pointed out the frequency of coffee shop trips by employees and pizza deliveries to the Rockstar offices have been monitored by fans, and traffic volumes by its workplaces were allegedly tracked in a bid to get an inside track on the GTA 6 release date.

articles.title: The Resident Evil Movie Understands Video Games Are Ridiculous, and That's Why It's Great
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie understands that video games are ridiculous, and that's why it's great.
articles.body:
Some very minor spoilers for Resident Evil (2026) follow:

Video games are ridiculous. The Resident Evil series is a perfect example of this. One moment you’re running in terror away from a comically oversized trench-coated tank of a man in a tiny hat; the next, you’re messing around with electronic chess pieces in order to open a door. These are completely alien situations that, somehow, these games make us feel compelled to navigate through rational thought. This is what Zach Cregger understands about Capcom’s genre-defining series so well. His Resident Evil movie knows that this is all ridiculous, and so the film has its lead, Brian, progress through its 90-minute rollercoaster just as we would if we had a controller in our hands. It’s a fantastic translation of the sensation that playing a survival horror game grants us, never forgetting to include every piece of glorious nonsense that comes with it.

Austin Abrams really is fantastic as Brian, a thoroughly normal guy thrust into a scenario he’s only ever seen on screens. “Video games!”, he shouts after solving a problem, almost surprising himself by the way video game logic has seeped into his mind and exploded into life in the real world. His original character is as close to a proxy for the viewer as you could wish for in a Resident Evil film, evoking the feeling we feel as players, rather than watching the events unfurl from the perspectives of established protagonists such as Chris Redfield or Leon Kennedy. That choice is the real masterstroke from Cregger, and it’s where so much of Resident Evil’s humour comes from.

When I visited the Prague set of the movie back in December of 2025 , the director told me, “It’s like if I were thrust into a Resident Evil video game. I’d be totally unequipped. I’m not good with guns. I’m totally out of shape. It would just be me panicking from one situation to another.” That description perfectly matches how Brian acts in the movie, hilariously bemoaning having to climb flights of stairs which stretch into the sky, running and screaming just long enough for terror to turn into humour, and self-proclaiming to be “not a gun guy,” despite having to learn on the job very quickly.

Brian stumbles his way through his journey to the heart of Raccoon City, never quite believing what he’s seeing happen in front of him. A combination of the unrelenting pace Cregger injects into the movie and the expressiveness of Abrams’ eyes make for laughs even in its most tense of moments. On the rare occasion that it does slow down for a beat, it's often to hold on Abrams' face as he attempts to take in exactly what shape of body horror he’s been subjected to witnessing next. He acts just like we do when playing the games, watching wide-eyed as whatever monster Capcom has concocted emerges from a freshly beheaded corpse. Normal logic would suggest you’d run straight for the door, as you likely would in real life. But in video games, you feel invulnerable, able to face up to the horrors presented to us. Cregger knows this feeling all too well from his repeat playthroughs of Resident Evil 4, a classic that most accurately hits the sweet spot in finding joyful absurdity in survival horror.

RE4’s opening village section has long been held as one of the most iconic introductions to any game. The delicate balance of creeping dread found in an all-too-quiet rural location is shattered by the tolling of bells and the sudden onrush of a population who have seen far better days. The Resident Evil movie sings from the same hymn sheet, steadily cranking up the tension before the action truly kicks off. This time, instead of a bell signalling a shift in tone, the bark and unearthly bite of a dog is the moment Brian knows things are about to get silly. He may not have the physical skills to pull off a Leon Kennedy-esque roundhouse kick to the head of an undead pensioner — again, this is a very silly video game series — but he does unload a shotgun blast into one that leaves their brain as nothing but red goo on a wall. Brian is having a bad time, but I’d be lying if I said much of the theater wasn’t laughing.

Cregger may only be three feature films deep into his career as a horror director, but already appears to have perfected the art of punctuating moments of terror with humour like this. It should come as no surprise to any who have seen either Barbarian or Weapons — two deeply unsettling movies at times, but also darkly hilarious when he chooses for them to be. The exact same can be said for Resident Evil, which, while never allowing Brian to shoot off quippy one-liners like Mr Kennedy would do, does give the character his fair share of funny moments, more often than not reflecting how we react when playing the games. You’re more likely to be faced with some sort of ungodly foe and find the word “damn” escaping from your mouth, as Brian does in one particularly funny moment, than speak in full sentences. It’s that reaction to the absurd from Abrams that carries the action so well, in many ways echoing the enjoyment that can be found in watching your favourite Twitch streamer play through a Resident Evil game, and the unscripted moments that come from it.

And let’s be honest: Much of the joy in watching other people play games can come from when things go wrong. Schadenfreude is a hell of a drug. Just as it can be funny when people fall off an arena when only one hit away from finishing off a boss, Resident Evil finds the fun in Brian’s failures. It’s much more interested in people being bad at their jobs rather than seasoned professionals — perhaps most keenly observed in how much more of the script is given to Paul Walter Hauser’s hapless company man than Kali Reis’ expert operative. There’s a fantastic running joke when it comes to Brian’s battle against padlocks — a very fun play on the Resident Evil games’ obsession with locked doors and the ludicrous methods of opening them. Here, instead of having to examine centuries-old paintings or slot precious gems into statues, he simply takes them on with a gun, often resulting in hilarious outcomes.

It’s just one example of how Cregger’s movie takes the essence of a Resident Evil game and plays with our expectations, all with the aim of making us laugh. It doesn’t quite completely resist the odd Easter egg item sitting in a room, but it is far more interested in translating the experience of playing the survival horror game than feeding fans little winks and nods. You can really tell that it comes from not only a deep love of Capcom’s games, but of video games in general and the ridiculous nature of them. Speaking of which, Cregger’s fun twist on a Resident Evil stalker enemy brings to mind the wondrous madness of Inside’s ending, which makes Playdead’s puzzle platformer so special, and the snowball-like splendour that powers the silliness behind the Katamari series.

Only video games regularly attempt to blend the mundanity of searching through every drawer in a house for shotgun shells to only moments later have to fire them into a creature unlike anything we’ve seen before, and then ask us to carry on as if nothing out of the ordinary just happened. This occurs dozens of times to Brian on his night through hell, and yet he perseveres, almost laughing off the absurdity of it all with us while evading death at every turn. That “video games!” he proclaims in that one rare moment of success may be spoken by Abrams, but feels directly delivered by Cregger to us. It sums up the movie perfectly, showing the filmmaker’s love for the, frankly silly, source material we all love so much.

Just like video games, Resident Evil is ridiculous, but in all the best ways. It’s an adaptation done in the right spirit, not interested in replicating a story beat-for-beat, but in trying, and succeeding, in reproducing the same joy we feel when playing through them. No, there’s no Mr. X here. But the same laugh you likely let out when you saw his tiny hat for the first time is more than present. And that’s the important part.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Xbox Aware of 'Phantom Achievement' Glitch That's Robbing Players of 100% Completion
articles.summary: Xbox fans report being blocked from 100% completion in various games due to so-called "phantom achievements" — despite having collected the full 1000 Gamerscore.
articles.body:
Xbox fans report being blocked from 100% completion in various games due to so-called "phantom achievements" — despite having collected the full 1,000 Gamerscore.

A bug is currently showing progress in some Xbox games capped below 100%, even when all visible achievements have been collected. For those who grind out achievements or who care about their count of games at 100% completion, this is an annoying glitch — especially as Xbox is believed to be working on an equivalent to PlayStation's Platinum trophy feature in future.

Thankfully, the cause of the issue appears to have already been tracked down, and Xbox is aware of the problem. Writing on X/Twitter, Xbox fan DarkIxion noted that the bugged games all seemed to be those with time-limited 0 Gamerscore challenges.

As a day one Xbox One purchaser, I remember the console's short-lived timed challenges, which provided extra achievements beyond each game's base list. Dead Rising 3, Titanfall, and Call of Duty: Ghosts had them, as did several non-gaming apps such as Netflix and YouTube.

Completing the requirements for these limited-time objectives would unlock exclusive bonus achievements — and while they provided 0 Gamerscore, they could also unlock extra game artwork or other in-game bonuses.

Alguns jogos que fiz 1000g no Xbox estão com uma conquista a mais, e não é a conquista de 0g. Vão acrescentar a "platina"? Verifiquem aí pic.twitter.com/hxEPeKc3LK — YT: Loredo Alles (@PiquenoLoredo) September 17, 2026

Alguns jogos que fiz 1000g no Xbox estão com uma conquista a mais, e não é a conquista de 0g. Vão acrescentar a "platina"? Verifiquem aí pic.twitter.com/hxEPeKc3LK

For those who missed out on a challenge, these 0G achievements did not appear in the game's main achievement list or count towards a game's 1,000 Gamerscore. But technically they were still attached to the game's data behind the scenes — something that this new bug is apparently surfacing.

"We're looking into why this changed," wrote Xbox engineering lead Eden Marie, responding to reports on Twitter/X. "Thanks for the report!"

Earlier this week, Microsoft insisted it was yet to "finalize" any changes to Xbox Game Pass , after a potential leak detailed plans to drop the inclusion of new titles from day one.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Player Glitches Out of Bounds to Discover Floating NPCs, Cars That Phase Through Walls, and the Edges of the Map
articles.summary: A Marvel’s Wolverine player has discovered a glitch that allows for out of bounds exploration right up to the edges of the map.
articles.body:
A Marvel’s Wolverine player has discovered a glitch that allows for out of bounds exploration right up to the edges of the map.

Warning! Spoilers for Marvel’s Wolverine follow…

A YouTuber called “ Turned ” published a video showing how Logan is able to climb up and over a seemingly innocuous building to go out of bounds in the mission, The One That Got Away. From there is a huge area to explore — much bigger than the linear play space would suggest — packed with all sorts of fun out of bounds gubbins, such as floating trees, ground that may or may not lead you under the map, and of course, glitchy collision. Turned makes their way to the boundaries of the map, where the ground squares off.

Youtuber Turned is demonstrating how there are glitches through which you can actually check the areas of map which were planned for the game. It seems like the game was much more ambitious at one point and scaled back to be a safer/smaller game. pic.twitter.com/I1DuAMb11a — eppy (@epppyyy) September 16, 2026

Youtuber Turned is demonstrating how there are glitches through which you can actually check the areas of map which were planned for the game. It seems like the game was much more ambitious at one point and scaled back to be a safer/smaller game. pic.twitter.com/I1DuAMb11a

Turned then published another video showing a similar out of bounds glitch in the Japan environment. By simply jumping over some trucks, Logan can leave the mission area and avoid triggering the automatic respawn.

There’s more fun glitchy stuff here, including cars that phase through walls. In the video, Turned follows the cars, which just keep driving straight forward until they despawn. What a sorry existence. The pedestrians don’t seem bothered though.

Things then get weirder — Turned explores buildings with no interior, views floating NPCs, and that old chestnut, the T-pose. The out of bounds areas for Japan are more detailed than the The One That Got Away mission, complete with eating areas and shops with interiors.

We’ve seen similar videos for countless video games over the years. In the last year or so, I’ve reported on out of bounds efforts in everything from Crimson Desert to The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered . But what’s remarkable here is the ease with which Turned is able to go out of bounds. It’s no surprise to see players discover these glitches when all you have to do is climb up a wall or jump over a vehicle. I suspect developer Insomniac will be keen to plug the gap sooner rather than later.

How do glitches like these make their way into a video game? TT Games developer Tim Spencer offered an explanation in a post on social media .

“FYI there's a 99% chance QA will have caught this, but someone in production will have dropped it to a priority 2 or lower, and during triage when they needed to ship: pushed it to a later patch (I don't want to think that they dropped it as WNF - ‘Will Not Fix’),” he said.

Earlier this week, Insomniac said it’s planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback . One aspect Insomniac may be looking at is Wolverine’s infamous “fart gas,” which has become the butt of online jokes in recent weeks . Some have called for Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game amid complaints about handholding.

articles.title: Resident Evil movie: Zach Cregger 'not prepared' for fan response
articles.summary: The video game adaptation is a hit with critics, but director Zach Cregger says the fan response surprised him.
articles.body:
One of the hottest horror directors on the planet adapting the world's most popular scary video game series?

On paper Zach Cregger and Resident Evil are the perfect unholy alliance.

The film-maker was widely praised for his original, imaginative work on horror hits Weapons and Barbarian and is a long-time fan of the video game series.

But in the lead-up to the film’s release, Cregger’s spent a lot of time defending himself against complaints he’s cashing in on the Resident Evil name.

Speaking to BBC Newsbeat, the director says he was "not prepared" for what came his way.

First launched in 1996 on the original Sony PlayStation by Japanese developer Capcom, Resident Evil was a sensation.

Rather than casting players as super-powered characters, as was the case with most video games in the 90s, it forced them to survive with limited resources.

Thanks to smart reinventions and remakes, the series has managed to stay relevant, selling a total of 213 million copies since its debut.

Some of its characters are among the most well-known in video games, and there are whole communities dedicated to discussing the lore of their universe.

Cregger's Resident Evil follows the story of Bryan, an original character played by Austin Abrams who worked with the director on Weapons.

He's a courier who agrees to deliver a package to a hospital in Raccoon City - a key location from the games.

As Bryan makes his way to the drop-off, it becomes apparent he is caught in the middle of some sort of viral outbreak, with the infected becoming monstrous creatures.

When the first trailer appeared online, many users swamped comment sections to complain about what they'd seen.

Where were the beloved characters? The familiar monsters?

Cregger says he had little interest in simply retelling the story of the Resident Evil games, but that didn't seem to calm some fans.

"I think I was expecting people to be excited to see a Resident Evil movie that felt in the spirit of the games.

"What I was trying to do is make a movie that really honoured the experience of playing them."

According to most reviews, Cregger has achieved what he set out to do.

In its three-star review, NME asked whether it was "the first great horror movie game adaptation".

"For a large chunk of the film's runtime, the answer is a resounding yes," wrote reviewer Jordan Bassett, who said Bryan's encounters become repetitive as the film wears on.

Doug Jamieson, of The Jam Report , awarded four stars and said Cregger "understands adaptation as translation rather than imitation".

In an eight out of 10 review, Looper critic Alastair Ryder wrote: "Zach Cregger has done the best job I've seen of translating the experience of playing a video game and making it feel cinematic."

The verdict from fans remains to be seen, but Resident Evil looks to be on track to have a successful opening weekend at the box office.

It follows recent video game adaptations such as the Minecraft and Super Mario Bros films, which were poorly reviewed but hugely popular.

This isn't the first adaptation of Resident Evil, which was brought to cinema screens in 2002 - the first of six films overseen by writer-director Paul WS Anderson.

His wife, Milla Jovovich, starred in each one, and while they have grown a cult following they were never a hit with critics.

A 2021 "reboot" heavily based on the games and a 2022 Netflix series also failed to impress.

The live-action rights to Resident Evil are owned by German production company Constantin Film - a fact fans have blamed for the perceived low quality of previous adaptations.

Reports online suggest the company's agreement with Capcom prevents Constantin from setting its films in the same timeline as the games.

Cregger told Newsbeat he'd had no contact with the game developer while working on the film.

"Nobody from Capcom ever reached out to me, ever, in any way," he said.

Constantin Film declined to comment, but BBC Newsbeat has been told there was co-ordination between the developer and the film's producers behind the scenes.

Cregger says it's "probably" impossible to please everyone, but it was never his intention to recreate the game on-screen.

"If I had delivered a faithful retelling of one of the stories in the games, I feel like those people would probably be upset with me for that too," he says.

"Because I would have messed it up somehow, inevitably.

"So all I can do is just tell the story that I think is going to be the very best story.

"If somebody's going to have a problem that it doesn't do exactly what they had in their mind of what a Resident Evil movie is, I can't say anything to that."

Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here .

articles.title: Control Resonant is Almost a Picture Perfect PC Port
articles.summary: Control Resonant is nearly a picture perfect PC port, with gorgeous visuals and stellar performance on almost every PC I've tested it on.
articles.body:
When the Nvidia GeForce RTX 2080 Ti first came out in 2018, I was skeptical of ray tracing and DLSS. The first few games that used the tech, like Battlefield 1 and Shadow of the Tomb Raider , had fairly lackluster ray tracing implementations that didn't look great and were just a way to nuke performance without getting much out of it. It wasn’t until Control came out in the summer of 2019 that it really started to click for me.

There was just something about the lighting solution for that game that made it look better than pretty much anything else out at the time, even if it wasn’t going for total realism. It’s no surprise then, that Control Resonant follows in the original game’s footsteps, and might just be one of the most beautiful games of the year because of it. But even with the incredible things Remedy was able to do with the visuals, Control Resonant is still one of the best optimized PC games of the year so far, and even runs reasonably well on the Xbox Ally X.

Remedy’s last game was certainly a technical masterpiece as well. Alan Wake 2 is still one of the most beautiful games I’ve ever seen, and there are parts of that game that look like I’m playing through a movie, especially on higher graphics settings. But at the same time, it’s not a game that’s known for running on less powerful PCs.

Control Resonant, though, dials back on some of the ultra realism of Alan Wake 2, and is able to scale much better to less powerful hardware. While the game definitely rewards high-end PCs with a stunning implementation of path tracing that really accentuates the game’s art style, it’s somehow even more impressive how good the game looks on a handheld.

When I downloaded the game on the Xbox Ally X , I honestly expected a mess after dealing with Halo: Campaign Evolved , Star Wars Zero Company , and to a lesser extent The Blood of Dawnwalker. But, as soon as I flipped on that handheld graphics preset and set FSR to quality, the game still looked great at 1080p, and I was able to get 40-45 fps in the first boss fight, even with all of the debris flying all over the place.

The game does drop to the mid-30s occasionally, but even when it does, it still feels smooth enough that I don’t feel like it’s causing me to be any worse at the game. I would prefer if it didn’t have these drops, of course, but at least it supports FSR frame generation, so I can fake 60+ fps, even if it comes at the expense of a bit of latency.

Control Resonant does make the Steam Deck show its age a bit, though. Even with the handheld preset, set to 720p and FSR set to balanced, Valve's four-and-a-half year old handheld struggles to stay above 25 fps. You can absolutely play the game like that if you want, but I wouldn't really recommend it.

Of course, if you do have more powerful hardware, the game runs extremely well on a full desktop system too. Remedy's official PC system requirements list the RTX 4070 Ti as its recommended GPU for playing the game at the medium preset, with ray tracing set to medium, expecting to get 60 fps. And, if anything it underestimated how well it runs.

I installed an RTX 4070 Ti Super and set the game to 1440p with the medium preset with ray tracing at medium, along with DLSS set to balanced. At those settings, Control Resonant averaged 111 fps, with a 1% low of 81 fps – far above Remedy's quoted 60 fps for those settings. Granted, I did test with an RTX 4070 Ti Super, which is around 10-15% faster than the recommended 4070 Ti. But even if you lopped off 15% of the frames there, it would still average 94 fps, which is better than Remedy's official system requirements suggest.

There's so much room to pump up the details, too. I wanted to see what would happen if I maxed out the game at 1440p with the same DLSS settings, and even at the Ultra preset with path tracing, the game averaged 70 fps with a 1% low of 58 fps. Again, if you take away 15% of the performance to account for the difference between the 4070 Ti Super and the 4070 Ti, you're still looking at around 60 fps. And that's all without even touching frame generation.

With frame generation enabled, the RTX 4070 Ti's frame rate jumps to 118 fps, although the pre-frame-gen number drops down to 60. Still, that is more than enough for Control Resonant to feel responsive, while also delivering an incredibly smooth frame rate for a high-refresh gaming monitor . Usually, turning on frame gen would come with more latency than having it off, but for some reason, Remedy doesn't include the option to turn on Nvidia reflex indepently from frame interpolation, so you actually end up with less latency with it enabled.

With how good the lighting is in Control Resonant, I probably would have come away happy if the game ran a lot worse than it does. The fact that it scales so well while looking as good as it does makes it one of the best PC ports of the year so far. If you have a halfway decent gaming PC lying around and you're planning on playing Resonant anyways, I'd recommend picking it up on Steam in a heartbeat.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.body:
Control Resonant from developer Remedy Entertainment is one of the more unique, anticipated releases of the last decade.

Sounds wild to say in a historically stacked 2026 calendar release year. But Resonant is the wished-for return to the world of Control, the classic from 2019.

It's also another return for Remedy, which is never shy about going away from what works. Sequels for Max Payne, Alan Wake and others left comfort zones for bold risks and repeatedly found ample success.

Hyrox Athlete Apologizes for Pooping Pants 🥴

Resonant joins the list. There's the mind-bending paranormal stuff, thankfully, but the story and backbone gameplay leave the comfort zone to try something new.

Like those before it, the risk could lead to another classic.

It's no easy feat for any game to one-up The Oldest House as a setting and all-time set pieces like The Ashtray Maze.

Yet here comes Resonant, its sequel , attempting just that.

Resonant looks good in the expected, flashy next-gen ways when it comes to graphics, lighting and the souped-up stuff like all the -tracings of the day. Character models are expressive, the physics are good and the soundtrack is fittingly spooky or tense when needed. Plus, again, expected, but great voice acting.

Resonant has decided to start at Oldest House, then zoom out, tackling a big chunk of Manhattan in the process. There's always a feel of fresh new areas and discomfort with every turn, as the ceiling can suddenly be the floor and many such reality-warping things happen. Like with Control, the setting here is very much a character in its own right and super memorable.

Whereas the 2019 effort largely focused its combat enough on weaponry and paranormal powers from range to classify as a third-person shooter, Resonant gets more nitty-gritty with a melee focus.

The main character's "Aberrant" is a shapeshifting weapon that starts with a few simple forms before morphing into something else entirely, with customizable secondary forms, combo-enders and more.

Like its predecessor, Resonant lets players cut loose with all types of powers, too. There's the tried-and-true "throw stuff from the surroundings" power. But there's also a ground slam, burns, shields and all sorts of other telepathic powers one might be able to dream up.

Encounters can happen in waves, too. It's not just clearing out an area anymore: Lesser enemies can keep respawning for more if players don't deal with the elite foes nearby. But that goes the other way, too: Players can skip the fluff and get the big bads, which auto-clears out the little guys.

There's a fun mix of things going on here. The floaty feel of Control's combat remains, but it's totally fair to throw out names like "Devil May Cry" while trying to sum up its parts. Either way, it's a fun, fast-paced romp and tough skill selections and weapon decisions will let players fine-tune the experience to their liking and style.

Overworld traversal is fun and made easy via fast travel points and unlockable movement abilities found in Faults, which are little challenges to complete. Otherwise, players are looking at multiple jumps, a glide and a dash they can chain, nothing unexpected.

The whole thing grows and expands alongside the player's own skill, which is an impressive feat. More to the point than anything else, though, it's just fun to get into the combat when not looking slack-jawed at the latest anomaly around every corner.

Dylan Faden is the protagonist here and he's searching for his sister, Jesse Faden, protagonist of the first game. Dylan happened to be from the first game too, though he's changed quite a bit, appearance-wise.

Dylan is cut loose by the Federal Bureau of Control (FBC), hoping he can help in downtown Manhattan, where some sort of yet-ununderstandable entity wreaks havoc.

There's a whole heap of backstory here that will make some excellent longform YouTube viewing. Point is, Dylan is quite a different personality than Jesse and doesn't necessarily want to make amends for his role in the events of the first game, but he'd really like to find his sister and help out those innocents impacted out in the city, too.

This is Remedy, so the story is captivating, the side characters memorable and the environmental storytelling has no equal in the industry.

There are things beyond the story, too. Side quests are out there and, as mentioned, this can include finding little activities to overcome that reward movement abilities. There are also vendors scattered about who offer up resources.

Progression hits expected notes. A leveling-up system that bumps overall power level through ability and Aberrant upgrades offers both power and customization to the experience. On top of refining skill trees and weapon choices, players can craft artifacts and pick and choose the buff-debuff options to take into the fray.

As a whole, there's a lite resource management and skill tree stuff going on here, in a good way. The system asks for some tough choices and encourages experimentation, which is a boon in its favor.

Resonant runs well and is packed with helpful options in the menus, including a full-blown assist mode that players can customize to their choosing.

Some of Control's greatest aspects, like the ambiance of the unknown, environmental storytelling and deep lorecrafting persist. But where the combat could have been "more Control," and the protagonist "more Jesse," Resonant goes a new way and finds a hit.

In all respects, Resonant is a feat of one-upmanship. It's a sequel done right and continues to dominate the supernatural niche Control commands. Bonus points: It's a Game of the Year contender, but has just the same decade-long staying power as the original.

articles.title: Resident Evil (2026) 4K Steelbook Is Up for Preorder
articles.summary: The new Resident Evil movie may have just hit theaters, but it's already up for preorder in a 4K steelbook edition that also includes a Blu-ray and digital copy.
articles.body:
Heads up, horror fans. Zach Cregger’s 2026 movie Resident Evil may have just hit theaters, but the 4K steelbook edition is already up for preorder ( see it at Amazon ). The MSRP is $44.99, and the release date is TBA, presumably depending on how the film does in cinemas around the world. Still, if you want this special edition, I would recommend preordering soon, because 4K steelbooks of popular movies often sell out well before release.

Resident Evil isn’t a typical adaptation of Capcom’s beloved video game franchise. Instead of adapting a story that’s already been told in a game, writer/director Zach Cregger wanted to make a movie that gives audiences the same feeling gamers have when playing the games.

It’s still set in a zombie-infested Raccoon City, but instead of telling the story of Leon, Claire, or co., it follows a medical courier named Bryan, who has a delivery that brings him to the doomed town. What follows is 95 minutes of undead mayhem, splashed with blood, gore, tension, and more than a little humor thrown in for good measure.

That’s about what I would expect from Cregger, who is also the creative driving force behind the exemplary horror movies Barbarian and Weapons , both of which go to very unexpected places. They both also blend horror and comedy in unique and, to my mind, exciting ways.

In IGN’s Resident Evil review , critic Tom Jorgensen gave it an 8/10, writing: “With a clear appreciation for odds stacked against the protagonist and all manner of freaky foes to stand against them, Cregger ably adapts the spirit, if not the letter, of the Resident Evil games into a jet-fueled horror experience that has room for lots of tension, some great laughs, and a strong central performance from Austin Abrams.”

As for what bonus material comes in this edition, it hasn’t been announced yet. When it is, I’ll add it to this article. In the meantime, you can check out the Resident Evil movies in order and, after watching the film, you can check out our ending explained .

Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, Saga Arts, and Fathom Entertainment announced Friday that tickets are now on sale online and at participating box offices for the 20th Anniversary theatrical re-release of V for Vendetta , which will be in theaters nationwide on November 1 and 5, 2026.

“The award-winning V for Vendetta graphic novel led to one of the most provocative films in the early 2000s. articles.title: This cartridge-playing Game Boy clone is smaller and cheaper than Analogue’s Pocket
articles.summary: The FPGB Mini is only slightly wider than the original Nintendo cartridges it plays.
articles.body: FunnyPlaying, a Chinese company known for its Game Boy and GBA upgrade kits, has announced a new handheld that plays original Nintendo cartridges and ROMs. The FPGB Mini’s cartridge support is limited to the Game Boy and Game Boy Color so it isn’t as capable as the Analogue Pocket that’s also compatible with the GBA and Sega Game Gear. What still makes the FPGB Mini a tempting alternative is its extremely pocketable design resulting in a handheld only slightly wider than a Game Boy cartridge, and its cheaper price. [Image: The FPGB Mini allows for multiplayer and trading over a USB-C cable. Following recent price hikes the Analogue Pocket is now $239.99 while the FPGB Mini is currently discounted from $89.99 to $69.99 for the first batch of just 20 units that quickly sold out. However, the company is potentially planning to release more following some hardware improvements, according to Retro Dodo who’s been testing the handheld for a few days and so far seems impressed with its design and capabilities. [Media: Like the Pocket the FPGB Mini uses field-programmable gate array (FPGA) technology to play Game Boy and GBC games as accurately as Nintendo’s original hardware does. But the FPGB Mini brings improvements like a 2.98-inch, 800x720-pixel LCD display, an 1,800mAh rechargeable battery, and a microSD slot for storing game saves, screenshots, or ROMs that can be played through emulation. The handheld’s compact size does prevent cartridges with rumble motors or other hardware additions from being used, but otherwise the FPGB Mini looks to be about as small as the Game Boy is ever going to get.

articles.title: Call of Duty Maker Activision Says the Video Game Cheat Market Generates $8.5 Billion a Year
articles.summary: Ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s release, Activision has spoken about the “multi-billion-dollar market” behind video game cheats.
articles.body:
Ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s release, Activision has spoken about the “multi-billion-dollar market” behind video game cheats.

Cheating is a fact of life in pretty much all online games, but Call of Duty has a reputation for it, exacerbated by the free-to-download battle royale, Warzone. Activision, like other video game companies, faces an uphill battle against cheaters and those who make and profit from them, and generative AI has made that battle even more complex.

Now, to hammer home the point about how big a deal video game cheating is, Activision's Team Ricochet has posted a blog that breaks down the business behind it.

“Cheat sellers have built a sprawling, multi-billion-dollar marketplace of resellers, subscription services, cheat reskins, illicit accounts, spoofing tools, and organized distribution networks,” Activision said, pointing to recent analysis that suggests cheat subscriptions across just 15 games generates roughly $3.5 billion annually. Activision estimates that when you include adjacent industries such as account sales, boosting, spoofing, and other services, the broader cheating economy generates about $8.5 billion each year.

You might have seen Activision post bodycam footage of a Call of Duty cheat maker being served a cease and desist order — that’s part of the legal action the company takes here. But it’s also using “technical detection” to try to clamp down on cheat makers.

RICOCHET Anti-Cheat doesn't end when your match does. Cheat makers operate around the world. So do we. We’re taking the fight directly to cheat sellers. Last weekend during the Closed Beta, we went to Ohio to takedown Elocarry. That’s not an isolated case... pic.twitter.com/IP69qlGgDD — Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) August 28, 2026

RICOCHET Anti-Cheat doesn't end when your match does. Cheat makers operate around the world. So do we. We’re taking the fight directly to cheat sellers. Last weekend during the Closed Beta, we went to Ohio to takedown Elocarry. That’s not an isolated case... pic.twitter.com/IP69qlGgDD

Activision said it’s “disrupted” more than 375 reseller operations, issued more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and helped shut down 31 primary cheat vendors. “Cheat sellers often use marketing tactics and social posts to make their operations look stable, even when they are under significant pressure,” Activision said. “We’ve seen cheat developers use social platforms to explain months of downtime with excuses like ‘the flu,’ ‘surgery,’ or a ‘car accident’ rather than acknowledge their products were detected and no longer reliable. Those messages are part of the playbook they use to reassure customers while our systems continue disrupting their networks.”

Activision also pointed out that cheating is getting more expensive off the back of pressure it’s applying to the ecosystem. But still, some of the figures it’s released are eye-watering. It said cheaters could spend more than $1,000 a year just to cheat, when you consider some subscription cheats can cost upwards of $100 on the higher end, and spoofers add another recurring fee. DMA-related hardware and services drive the cost even more.

“Over the course of one year, some players spend hundreds of dollars — if not thousands — trying to maintain access to cheats, evasion tools, and replacement accounts,” Activision said. “Ultimately, cheating is a losing investment. Every time we identify and remove a bad actor, the money they spent cheating goes with them — all for a temporary ego boost.”

As always, the proof of the pudding is in the eating. Most accept Activision will never stamp cheating out of Call of Duty entirely, but the hope is that it will be less prevalent in Modern Warfare 4 than it has been in previous years.

Earlier this month, IGN interviewed David Andrews, Senior Director of Game Security for Call of Duty, to dispel some myths about Call of Duty cheating — and the work Activision does to prevent it.

Halo: The Fall of Reach was first released back in 2001, launching a couple weeks before the first Halo game came out in November of that year. Serving as the official prequel to the series, Eric Nylund's novel tells the story of how Master Chief came to be and what led to the events of Halo: Combat Evolved .

Since the book's original release 25 years ago, it has received several revised versions and editions. And now for the first time ever, it's getting the full-cast audio treatment thanks to Simon & Schuster Audio. You can check out IGN's exclusive audio clip for an idea of what to expect.

The voice cast includes Steve Downes and Jen Taylor reprising their roles as Master Chief and Cortana. It also includes an immersive sound experience that integrates things like the Halo theme song and the ridiculous sounds of Grunts running away terrified. Here's the official story description from the publisher page :

"The twenty-sixth century. Humanity has expanded beyond Earth’s system to hundreds of planets that colonists now call home. But the United Earth Government and the United Nations Space Command is struggling to control this vast empire. After exhausting all strategies to keep seething colonial insurrections from exploding into a full-blown interplanetary civil war, the UNSC has one last hope. At the Office of Naval Intelligence, Dr. Catherine Halsey has been hard at work on a top-secret program that could bring an end to the conflict…and it starts with seventy-five children, among them a six-year-old boy named John. And Halsey could never guess that this child will eventually become the final hope against an even greater peril engulfing the galaxy—the inexorable confrontation with a theocratic military alliance of alien races known as the Covenant."

If you're new to audiobooks, there's an Audible free trial worth checking out that can get you access to The Fall of Reach at no cost. Audible launched its new Standard subscription plan earlier this year that gets you your first audiobook for free.

Considering this book doesn't come out until November, that's a great option if you want to get access to some of the best audiobooks before this title officially releases.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Has 'Sold Well,' Early Data Suggests, but Don't Expect Spider-Man Numbers
articles.summary: Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
articles.body:
Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine , but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.

Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, took to social media to say an estimated 22.9% of that revenue came from the sale of physical copies of the game — remember, Sony plans to cease production of PlayStation discs from 2028.

Through all this, it’s important to note that Sony has yet to make any official sales announcement for Marvel’s Wolverine. It has made sales announcements for PlayStation Studios games in the past. For example, Sucker Punch’s Ghost of Yotei went on sale on October 2, 2025 and sold 3.3 million units as of November 2 (at the 32 day mark), according to Sony’s official figures.

Back in October 23, Sony announced that Insomniac's PlayStation 5 exclusive Spider-Man 2 sold more than 2.5 million copies in 24 hours , which meant the open-world superhero game overtook Santa Monica Studio’s God of War Ragnarok at the top of the PlayStation day-one launch sales chart. At the time, it was the fastest-selling PlayStation Studios game in history (Helldivers 2 now holds top spot).

Assuming Alinea Analytics is in the right ballpark, Marvel’s Wolverine is tracking behind Spider-Man 2. But it has already passed the lifetime PS5 copies sold and revenues of Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding 2, which hit the headlines when Sony ditched Kojima’s Physint. Indeed, according to Elliot, Marvel’s Wolverine is after just a few days on sale the top-performing new PlayStation Studios game released on PS5 so far this year, ahead of MLB The Show, Bungie’s Marathon, Housemarque’s Saros, and fighting game Marvel Tōkon.

The big question is how well Wolverine continues to sell. Wolverine is currently sitting on a 77 Metascore , with IGN’s Marvel’s Wolverine review returning a 6/10. We said: “Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay.”

“So yes, Wolverine has sold well, but its commercial long tail is limited by its mixed media and streamer reception,” Elliott said. “Unlike Spider-Man, which reviewed insanely well and has stayed evergreen for years, this one’s tail will be shorter and lumpier, but still there.”

Expect a bump when the MCU kicks into gear this December with the release of Avengers: Doomsday, which features the X-Men (but does it feature Hugh Jackman’s Wolverine?). Wolverine might also benefit from the expanded PS5 install base that will inevitably kick in with the release of GTA 6 in November. And Wolverine is sure to prove a popular choice under the Christmas tree.

“Wolverine will keep selling, just not at Spider-Man heights,” Elliott added. “Spidey’s been evergreen. Wolverine will be more ever-yellow.”

Earlier this week, Insomniac said it was planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback . One aspect Insomniac may be looking at is Wolverine’s infamous “fart gas,” which has become the butt of online jokes in recent weeks . Some have called for Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game amid complaints about handholding.

We’ve got 17 Essential Tips and Tricks to help you get started in Marvel’s Wolverine, plus our recommendations for the 10 Best Adaptations , and a guide on How to Farm XP Quickly . Check out our full Marvel’s Wolverine Walkthrough for a step-by-step guide to every mission, and make sure you don’t miss a thing with our Collectibles guides, All Wolverine Suits and Claws Guide , and our thorough list of all the Easter Eggs and References we've found.

articles.title: PlayStation’s Creative Future Has Never Looked Bleaker - IGN
articles.summary: Cutting ties with Kojima and poor Wolverine reviews are just the latest issues in a difficult generation for PlayStation. The platform's creartive future has never looked bleaker. It’s impossible to know how PlayStation bosses felt after seeing many critics walk away from Insomniac’s Wolverine with an apathetic shrug. A sub-80 on Metacritic is infamously considered a disaster in the triple-A space, and so Sony certainly won’t be thrilled, but it would be easy for the company to brush this away as an uncharacteristic miss.
