articles.title: Former PlayStation Execs Recreate Iconic Disc-Sharing Xbox Diss — Without the Physical Games This Time
articles.summary: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic game-sharing instructional video as Sony helps the industry barrel toward a discless future.
articles.body:
Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic game-sharing instructional video as Sony helps the industry barrel toward a discless future.

Even if you weren't playing too many games in 2013, there's a good chance you remember the "Official PlayStation Used Game Instructional Video." It was a viral 20-second how-to that saw then-Sony figureheads Boyes and Yoshida deliver a tongue-in-cheek guide for sharing physical games on PS4, racking up 21.3 million YouTube views in the 13 years since its premiere.

At the time, Sony took a clear and successful jab at Microsoft and its rocky Xbox One launch plans. Fast forward 13 years, and Sony's plan to kill physical discs will have game sharing on PlayStation looking quite different from 2028 . With the end of physical discs looming, Boyes and Yoshida reunited to recreate the legendary moment at Tokyo Game Show, and unfortunately, there were no physical games to be found.

Met with a best friend :D @amboyes @PlayStation_jp #TGS2026 pic.twitter.com/2ZjsrLMNaP — Shuhei Yoshida (@yosp) September 18, 2026

"Met with a best friend," Yoshida said with an open-smile emoticon.

The two snapped a few photos together as part of Tokyo Game Show, calling back to the moment that has lived rent-free in gamers' heads for years. It was clearly a fun nod to PlayStation's past, but the future is looking grim, and fans have mixed feelings.

"This picture of Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes from Tokyo Game Show is making the rounds," physical game X/Twitter account @DoesItPlay1 said . "Seemingly mocking current anti-consumer PlayStation for killing the philosophy behind their once famous pro-consumer mockery of Xbox regarding physical game sharing."

"This is how you share games with your friends in 2028," another fan added , referencing the lack of games in their hands.

How it started / How it ended pic.twitter.com/pXBz5lUbQQ — JayRock (@JayDaR0ck) September 18, 2026

How it started / How it ended pic.twitter.com/pXBz5lUbQQ

I know what you did there. pic.twitter.com/d6AztR0uIC — SJ89 (@Shehryar16) September 18, 2026

I know what you did there. pic.twitter.com/d6AztR0uIC

2013 vs 2026 🥲 13 ans plus tard, Shuhei Yoshida recrée sur son compte Twitter sa photo iconique de l’E3 2013… sauf que cette fois, lui et son collègue ne s’échangent que du vent ! #TokyoGameShow #PlayStation pic.twitter.com/fkJEq5yu2L — PSI (@PSInsideFr) September 18, 2026

2013 vs 2026 🥲 13 ans plus tard, Shuhei Yoshida recrée sur son compte Twitter sa photo iconique de l’E3 2013… sauf que cette fois, lui et son collègue ne s’échangent que du vent ! #TokyoGameShow #PlayStation pic.twitter.com/fkJEq5yu2L

Sony announced in July of this year that it would cease physical disc production for new video games starting in January 2028. It's a move that has landed the PlayStation company in hot water for months , and despite recently soft sales for game discs , the topic isn't something fans plan to let go anytime soon.

But in July, Sony insisted its decision wasn't having any impact on its business , and it didn't predict any negative impact in the future, either. When Sony announced the news it said it was simply following consumer trends. “In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only,” Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog .

There are of course instances of companies reversing controversial decisions amid a backlash, but, as analysts have told IGN , it remains unlikely that Sony will U-turn on this. For Sony, going all-digital for new game releases will earn it more money from every sale at a time when console sales are expected to plummet due to their rising cost.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

For a first-party PlayStation game such as Marvel's wolverine, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%.

articles.title: Scalpers Are Trying to Sell Valve's Steam Frame for Up to $2,000, but the Community Is Fighting Back
articles.summary: After putting up the Steam Frame for reservation on Monday, Valve has finally sent out its emails letting people know if they're on the reservation list or on the waitlist for the new VR headset. And, predictably, scalpers are already listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay.
articles.body:
After putting up the Steam Frame for reservation on Monday, Valve has finally sent out its emails letting people know if they're on the reservation list or on the waitlist for the new VR headset. And, predictably, scalpers are already listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay.

While Valve lists the 256GB Steam Frame kit for $1,059, the eBay listings start at $1,700 for the lower storage tier. If you want to get the 1TB model, that's being listed at around $2,000 by scalpers, despite Valve's $1,299 asking price.

What's especially egregious about these listings is that the Steam Frame is already expensive for what it is, due to the ongoing RAM crisis . While I'd have some wiggle room for a VR headset with Valve's open platform and incredible wireless PCVR, I'm not sure I'd spend that much money on something without OLED optics.

Unfortunately, it looks like at least some of these listings have already sold.

Luckily, the community is fighting back. Folks on the /r/steam subreddit are mobilizing to report these listings, and it seems like eBay is taking action. After sharing instructions on how to report these listings, user /u/obscenemexican added: "Update: I'm now getting flooded with emails from eBay that the reported content has been removed, huzzah! Many down, many more to go, keep it up guys!"

Meanwhile, other users in the thread have found some of the scalpers' Steam usernames in the eBay listings and have reported them to Valve. User /u/noonyIRL said: "If you want to hurt these scum more, contact them and ask for the Steam ID tied to the reservation to check their VAC/Ban status to ensure its legitimate. If they provide it, report them to Valve, if they refuse, report to eBay for failing to provide suitable evidence. Either way, this hits their account, not just their listing."

Valve did try to mitigate the risks of scalpers when it released both the Steam Machine and the Steam Frame, implementing a random lottery system tied to its preorders. When the Frame was announced on Monday, Valve opened up a sign-up system, where anyone with a Steam Account could select which version of the headset they were interested in. Then, Valve randomized the entries and split them into a bucket of reservations and a waitlist.

I'm sure that did mitigate how many scalpers would otherwise be able to get the system if it was available on a first-come, first-serve basis, but it clearly did not stop scalpers from trying to profit off of the system's scarcity. Hopefully, either eBay, Valve or both get this situation under control, so that more people are able to get the Frame at a somewhat reasonable cost.

articles.title: Marvel Drops a Massive Avengers: Armageddon Twist, as [Spoiler] Finally Enters the Stage
articles.summary: In a twist that's been 17 years in the making, Marvel has finally introduced [Spoiler] in the pages of Avengers: Armageddon. Here's why that's such a big deal.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains full spoilers for Avengers: Armageddon #4!

Marvel has spent months teasing the idea that Avengers: Armageddon will radically reshape the Avengers franchise and the Marvel Universe as a whole. With the penultimate chapter of Armageddon now on the stands, we now have a better idea of what that entails. This issue introduces a huge new character to the playing field, one fans have been waiting years to see. That's right, Miracleman has finally joined the Marvel Universe.

Who is Miracleman, and why is his debut such a big deal? Here's everything you need to know about the character and why he promises to profoundly shake things up heading into 2027.

Miracleman was originally known as Marvelman. He was created by writer/artist Mick Anglo in 1954, appearing in comics published by the British company L. Miller & Son. L. Miller & Son had previously found success republishing Fawcett Comics' Captain Marvel comics, but after losing the rights to that franchise, they commissioned Marvelman as a replacement character.

Conceptually, Marvelman is very similar to Captain Marvel/Shazam. When an ordinary but morally upright young man named Mickey Moran utters the word "Kimota," he transforms into a powerful superhero. Also like Captain Marvel, Marvelman had younger sidekicks aiding him in his battles against evil, in this case Young Marvelman and Kid Marvelman.

Marvelman fell into obscurity and vanished from the stands in the mid-'60s. It wasn't until Warrior Magazine revived the property in the early '80s that Marvelman reached a new audience and a much larger level of critical acclaim. Warrior tasked a young Alan Moore with reimagining Marvelman. This new version, which came to be known as Miracleman, dramatically revamped the character to become a much darker, more mature figure heavily influenced by the writings of Friedrich Nietzsche.

Under Moore and artists like Garry Leach, Alan Davis, Chuck Austen, and Rick Veitch, Miracleman became a hot property and one of the vanguards of a more literary approach to superhero comics in the '80s. After Moore wrapped up his 16-issue run, the series was taken over by Neil Gaiman and Mark Buckingham. Unfortunately, the collapse of publisher Eclipse Comics in the early '90s cut their planned story short.

Following Eclipse's bankruptcy, Marvelman/Miracleman remained trapped in limbo for decades, sparking a prolonged legal battle between Gaiman and Todd McFarlane Productions. It wasn't until 2009 that Marvel discovered the original ownership rights actually still resided with Anglo. They purchased the character from Anglo and began reprinting the classic stories in 2010. In 2022, they also launched Miracleman: The Silver Age, allowing Gaiman and Buckingham to continue their long-dormant collaboration. However, in light of the sexual assualt allegations against Gaiman , it doesn't appear that Marvel has any current plans to finish off that trilogy by publishing Miracleman: The Dark Age.

Since 2009, Miracleman fans have been dying to know what Marvel's long-term plans for the character are. While they slowly reprinted the classic books and continued Gaiman and Buckingham's Miracleman saga, it was also understood that some version of the character would be integrated into the larger Marvel Universe. But apart from one brief tease in 2021's Timeless #1, no hint of Miracleman has been seen in the Marvel U. At least, until now.

Avengers: Armageddon #4 reveals that Miracleman has been hiding in plain sight for the past couple of years. His atomic power now resides within the body of David Colton, a character who was recently introduced in Chip Zdarsky's Captain America run as the forgotten post-9/11 Captain America .

Originally, Colton had powers similar to those of Steve Rogers. But when he was mortally wounded in the miniseries Wolverine: Weapons of Armageddon, Wolverine chose to save his life by activating an Origin Box (artifacts containing the stolen powers of various heroes and villains from the new Ultimate Universe). It was never clear just which Origin Box Colton bonded with, but it saved his life and bestowed Superman-esque powers on him.

Armageddon has explored the chaos that unfolds when the newly empowered David Colton chooses to use his powers to forcibly make the world a safer place. With help from Bucky Barnes, Colton destroyed the world's nuclear weapon stockpiles in issue #3. We learn in issue #4 that Colton was honoring the memory of his mother, an anti-war activist who never approved of him joining the military.

Naturally, the world hasn't responded well to forcible disarmament, with Russia unleashing its secret, off-the-books stockpile of warheads on the US and dispatching Red Hulk and the Winter Guard to bring down Colton and Bucky. Colton is again severaly injured in the ensuing battle. Plagued by visions of his mother, Colton finally understands the true nature of his powers and utters the secret word to unlock his final form.

Colton then transforms into Miracleman, emerging rejuvenated and achieving his true power at last. There's still one issue of Avengers: Armageddon left, so we'll see exactly how the revitalized Miracleman manages to pull the world back from the brink of total war. But we do know that the series ends with the Avengers being disgraced and going underground, paving the way for a very different team in Zdarsky and Marco Checchetto's relaunched Avengers comic . Meanwhile, Storm is set to spearhead a new team of X-Men to fill the void left by Earth's Mightiest Heroes.

Marvel has now confirmed that Miracleman is the sixth, previously unrevealed member of the underground Avengers team. They've also released the final version of Checchetto's cover art for the first issue:

Miracleman's presence will certainly give the team a major power boost in a time when they could clearly use it. But Marvel is also teasing that this debut is part of a much bigger and very long-term story Zdarsky is telling. The new description for The Avengers #1 reads:

In the aftermath of Armageddon, the world has turned its back on Earth’s Mightiest Heroes—but it may need them now more than ever as the devil has come to collect his due! When a demonic invasion erupts on Earth, CAPTAIN MARVEL, SPIDER-MAN, DAREDEVIL, WOLVERINE, LUKE CAGE and MIRACLEMAN assemble to save a world that no longer trusts them. But the unpredictable David Colton may not be able to be trusted with his godlike new abilities. And when gods cry war…the world may pay the price.

One thing is clear - Miracleman is a character with an important legacy and a certain expectation of storytelling quality. The Moore run in particular is still widely regarded as one of the best superhero comics ever published. After all these years of waiting for Miracleman to appear in the Marvel Universe, we'd hope that Marvel has a clear plan for how to use the character and how to live up to that lofty standard.

What do you think of Miracleman's long-awaited Marvel Comics debut? Vote in our poll and let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.body:
Toys 'R' Us, the once-ubiquitous toy store/mecca for 1980s kids, is set to open 120 new standalone stores this holiday season, the company announced. The expansion is in partnership with the Go! Retail Group, who first partnered with Toys 'R' Us owner WHP Global three years ago to begin the toy store back from the dead and back into retail life. There are currently 40 standalone stores nationwide as well as other locations inside select Macy's locations nationwide.

"This is a major moment for Toys 'R' Us as we significantly expand our presence across the United States," said WHP Global Executive Vice President Jamie Uitdenhowen. "Together with our incredible partners, we are growing Toys' R' Us in unique ways to meet customers wherever they are, whether that's at a standalone store in their hometown, inside Macy's, at the airport or at a Navy Exchange."

"This holiday season represents an extraordinary expansion for Toys 'R' Us in the US, and we couldn't be more excited to bring the magic of Toys'R'Us to so many communities across the country," said Gideon Schlessinger, CEO of Go! Retail Group. "There's something special about walking into a Toys'R'Us store, especially during the holidays — the excitement of discovering the hottest toys, seeing favorite brands and characters come to life, and finding that perfect gift."

This 40-something writer has fond memories wandering the seemingly endless aisles of toys in the store as a kid – in particularly the video game aisle, which had the game box art on the walls and tickets below each one, which you'd take to a special counter if you wanted to buy the game and they'd get the real thing from a lockup area in the back for you. But the Toys 'R' Us revival will attempt to modernize the chain as well.

"Select locations will introduce new experiences at the intersection of play, entertainment and content creation, including Creator Studios, dedicated spaces where influencers, creators and toy brands can create content, unveil new products and host toy reveals, launches and special events," the company said. "Select stores will also feature candy shops and cafés, giving customers even more reasons to explore, discover and spend time at Toys 'R' Us."

articles.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Surpasses Sonic the Hedgehog 3 to Become Highest-Rated Video Game Movie of All Time
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is out today, and it's already the highest-rated video game movie of all time on Rotten Tomatoes.
articles.body:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is out today, and it's already the highest-rated video game movie of all time on Rotten Tomatoes.

The scores are in, and at least as far as the review-aggregating website is concerned, the latest shot at a live-action adaptation of Capcom's beloved survival horror series has received the best reaction of any game movie to date. Resident Evil, which was directed by Weapons' Cregger and stars Austin Abrams, boasts a 96% critics' rating at the time of this story's publication, placing it multiple percentage points above a shortlist of other well-received adaptations, including Sonic the Hedgehog 3 ( 86% ), Werewolves Within ( 86% ), and The Angry Birds Movie 2 ( 72% ).

Video games have a long history of what has been deemed by many to be mediocre releases. Although many of those — including 2001's Tomb Raider and 1993's Super Mario Bros. — arrived early in the industry's life, recent years have had their fill of poorly received projects, too. Both Five Nights at Freddy's movies , despite pulling in plenty of love from audiences, failed to impress critics, and 2024's Borderlands fell just 11 places short of being the worst-rated video game movie of all time. What we're saying is that it's not exactly been stiff competition for Resident Evil, but don't let that dampen its impact.

Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond

Despite Cregger making a splash with his last two horror movies, the director has faced an uphill battle with his latest flick. Fans expecting the movie to stick closer to the lore were let down to see Abrams playing an original character in a live-action Raccoon City that looked a bit different than they may have been hoping for . Instead of Leon S. Kennedy, Nemesis, or any other familiar elements, the live-action Resident Evil instead opted to focus on new character Bryan in a story inspired by the feeling of playing the games rather than their stories.

"I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing," Cregger said during a recent conversation with IGN . "I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?"

It's been controversial, to say the least, but despite the online backlash that's seeped into Cregger's world, the critics aren't the only ones finding something to love about Resident Evil. After more than 500 verified ratings, Rotten Tomatoes has recorded a staggering 91% score from audiences. Whatever hangups you may have thought audiences would have going in, it seems the film has proven too good for most to deny.

"My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there," Cregger added during his talk with IGN. "This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story."

Resident Evil is still just getting its feet wet when it comes to its reception, so only time will tell if it will continue to be seen in a positive light in the weeks, months, and years ahead. It's undeniably a strong start, though, with the project also expected to clear the franchise's box office record .

IGN gave it a solid rating, too, awarding it an 8/10 review . We said, "With a laser focus on putting its hero through the worst night of his life, Resident Evil is a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities."

articles.title: The 10 Coolest Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration Cards
articles.summary: Here's our top 10 picks for the coolest and most artistically inspired Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration cards we've found so far, including Jirachi, Mew, Sylveon, and a few other budget-friendly fan favorites.
articles.body:
The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration expansion is easily one of the most artistically diverse collections in Pokémon TCG history.

From brand-new card rarities with pearlescent finishes to nostalgic reprints of iconic classics, this set has something for every kind of collector.

I've put together a list of my personal favourites, with the main criteria being artistic value and overall coolness.

Hisuian Zoroark - ME: 30th Celebration (30C)

Although playability and collector demand are always worth considering, I focused mainly on the creativity, originality, and visual impact of the card artwork, alongside the reception it’s had from fans.

The best thing is that there are plenty of options to meet everyone's needs, regardless of budget; whether you’re hunting pocket monsters with pocket change or looking for top-end chase cards!

Before we jump in, for those after boosters, our best suggestion is to request an invite from Amazon for the ETB at least , priced much more reasonably compared to other retailers. Invites will be sent out soon!

10. Pikachu ex — ME: 30th Celebration #149/128

While both Pikachu ex cards in this subset work together as a matching daytime and nighttime set, the "day" version illustrated by kantaro ever so slightly edges it out for me.

Not only is it cheaper—sitting at roughly $89.03 on TCGplayer compared to its nighttime equivalent bringing in $116.07—it features one of my favorite Pokémon of all time in the background: Espeon!

This is one of those pieces of art that has instantly come to represent the 30th Celebration set, making it an absolute gem for any anniversary collection.

9. Hisuian Zoroark — ME: 30th Celebration #123/128

I’m a huge Witch Hat Atelier fan, so when I heard artist and creator Kamome Shirahama was illustrating one of the coolest Pokémon—Hisuian Zoroark—I knew this card had to be mine. Shirahama brought her signature intricate linework and sweeping dark-fantasy flair to celebrate the card game's 30th milestone, making this illustration feel like a high-end art piece at an accessible market price of just $1.25 on TCGplayer. This one went straight into my basket!

8. Pikachu — ME: 30th Celebration #029/128

There are so many cool Pikachu variations floating around this expansion thanks to the each 30th Celebration booster pack guaranteeing one of these 30 unique foil Pikachu rare cards. However, my favorite has to be this one from Pokémon Art Director James Turner.

Turner was a massive creative driving force who brought the world of Generation 8 and its First Partner Pokémon to life. His instantly recognizable pop-art illustration style filled me with so much joy in his independent game, The Plucky Squire, and it’s so nice to see him return to Pokémon with this quirky, adorable design. Best of all, it sits at a super budget-friendly $1.48 market average on TCGplayer.

7. Alolan Exeggutor — ME: 30th Celebration #129/128

Alolan Exeggutor is one of the goofiest regional variants out there, and I love it. This card brings that absurdity to life - a towering palm tree looking down at you in a beachy Alolan scene. Artist AYUMI ODASHIMA does a fantastic job of leaning into just how silly this Mon is, going for a modest $3.50 median market price on TCGplayer.

6. Mew ex — ME: 30th Celebration #152/128

This Special Illustration Rare by Kuroimori is one of the most popular chase cards in the collection. It shows Mew resting in a lush, sun-dappled forest, bathed in soft ambient light and surrounded by wild honeysuckle. Considering Mew holds such a sacred place in the series' history as the first-ever Mythical Pokémon (and arguably the DNA root of the entire Pokédex!), it’s no surprise this card isn’t cheap - a hefty $231.14 market price on TCGplayer.

5. Lapras — ME: 30th Celebration #131/128

Everything about this piece feels like a warm vacation breeze. Artist Amelicart serves up gorgeous, sun-kissed ocean waves featuring a content Lapras gliding through the water alongside an adorable Spheal—which just happens to be one of my absolute personal favorite Pokémon! It's serene, atmospheric, and easily worth its $19.98 average market price on TCGplayer.

4. Meowth — ME: 30th Celebration #144/128

I love the way Meowth is completely slonked out over the staircase bannister in this piece by artist OKUBO. This scene is all too familiar to anyone who lives with cats - I have three of my own, and at any given chance, at least one of them is pulling this exact liquid-cat move across the furniture. This is definitely one I’ll be trying to get, sitting at $28.53 on TCGplayer at time of writing.

3. Sylveon ex — ME: 30th Celebration #153/128

If there’s one thing you know about me, it’s that I’m Eevee’s number one fan. So as soon as I saw this gorgeous Sylveon card, I immediately wanted it. Artist You Iribi delivers an unbelievably sleek, stylish illustration of Sylveon ex framed by soft ribbons and pastel light shifts.

The price isn’t as bad as you’d think for a card of this popularity - it’s currently at an average market price of $89.63 on TCGplayer. It’s not great, but that’s where this hobby is at nowadays.

2. Maushold — ME: 30th Celebration #146/128

I’m a little biased, as I’ve fallen in love with my Population Bomb spamming machine in Pokémon Champions. But this card is just pure, unadulterated fun! Artist osare captures the wholesome family energy of so many Mausholds going about their day, waving at you. How can you not love this? It’s hovering around a comfortable $36.44 market price on TCGplayer, but shifting quickly.

1. Jirachi ex — ME: 30th Celebration #155/128

This Jirachi card is simple stunning! Legendary TCG illustrator AKIRA EGAWA delivers what might genuinely be their masterwork with this Special Illustration Rare. Featuring cosmic, starry lighting, ethereal brushwork, and a sweeping sense of galactic scale, Jirachi ex looks less like a trading card and more like a museum-tier oil painting. Sitting at an average market price of $98.18 on TCGplayer, this might genuinely be one of the coolest Pokémon cards of all time, let alone the 30th Celebration.

No matter your favorite card in the 30th Celebration expansion, there’s something out there for everyone! Let me know what your personal coolest card is, and what you’re chasing in the comments. If you’re struggling to get your hands on any 30th Celebration products, make sure you have IGNDeals on notifications on X to be alerted to any new product drops.

Sara Heritage is a freelance journalist for IGN, specialising in Pokémon TCG. When she's not gaming, you’ll probably find her building yet another LEGO set she absolutely did not need, or chaining ranked matches in Pokémon Champions.

articles.title: Mega Man: Dual Override Preview: We Played as Proto Man This Time
articles.summary: Proto Man offers a distinctly different challenge than Mega Man. Not necessarily harder, just different. It’s worth noting that you won’t be switching back and forth between the two; at the start of your playthrough you’ll select which character to control for the entire run, offering some potential replayability to see the game both ways. I’m particularly curious about the various chips that can be unlocked, how those will affect gameplay, and what sort of moveset a fully upgraded Proto Man will have at his disposal. For that, I’ll have to wait for Mega Man: Dual Override’s launch, scheduled for Spring 2027.
articles.body:
Our Gamescom preview focused on playing as Mega Man, but this time we played as Proto Man.

Proto Man isn’t just a reskin of Mega Man with a cool scarf.

The demo’s boss fight against Twinkle Girl was tough but fair, thus exactly fitting into the Mega Man formula.

2027 is a big year for Mega Man. Everyone’s favorite little blue robot turns the big 40. That’s a major milestone, and few active franchises in all of gaming can celebrate that kind of longevity. As part of the festivities, we are getting a new mainline entry in the series in Mega Man: Dual Override. At Tokyo Game Show 2026 we had a chance to go hands-on in this robotic adventure, and found a traditional 2D shooter/platformer like the series is best known for, but with some modern twists.

Similar to Simon Cardy’s excellent preview , I would be taking on Twinkle Girl, and her lineup of stages. But this time, I’d be ditching the Blue Bomber in favor of his older brother, occasional foe, and sometimes ally Proto Man. For those who don’t know, Proto Man was the first of Dr. Light’s sentient robot creations, who long ago abandoned the good doctor to forge his own path. He’s flawed, a bit aloof, and cool as hell. Just look at those built in sunglasses!

Levels are now divided into distinct segments of ascending difficulty. Twinkle Girl’s area is themed after some sort of Robot World’s Fair, with colorful balloons ascending into the blue skies, and cheery, upbeat music pumping through my headphones in this first portion. After so many games returned to the depressing all brown and gray color palette of the late 2000’s, I haven’t to admit the vibrant colors are pretty refreshing.

Proto Man isn’t just a reskin of Mega Man with a cool scarf. Shots from his Proto Buster hit hard, but only travel a short distance ahead, and his charge shots arc out in a semi-circle slash attack, rather than send a big ball of energy all the way across the screen. His blaster also builds up heat, which can interfere with his attacks if he overheats. This dissipates over time or can be manually vented. It’s a different, in-your-face playstyle that needs timing and aggression to push through the enemy robots that litter the path ahead.

Mega Man: Dual Override – TGS 2026 Proto Man Screenshots

I quickly make my way though the first area, blasting through enemies, destroying wall-mounted turrets, and jumping over some indoor fireworks emitters (which seems like a firecode violation.) Each area ends with a boss, and the first, Big Press Don, alternates between flying in the air, then trying to land on me to crush me into robot-paste, or shooting a fist out of a chest cavity, both of which I use the classic Mega Man slide move to evade, and blast/slash ol’ Donny boy into early retirement.

Beating Dom lets me advance, but it also earns me a Bolt. These are essential; similar to Mega Man 11, these feed into Dr. Light’s lab, which in turn allows you to unlock Custom Chips, which can be equipped and used to boost your performance. I didn’t get to unlock any in my run, but I did come equipped with a rapid-fire chip that let Proto Man unleash a torrent of machinegun-like blasts from his Proto Gun, which could quickly turn most enemies to scrap. Bolts are also hidden in each of the levels, offering incentive to explore thoroughly, and I could see myself farming any Bolts I was missing if I got stuck on a particularly hard boss.

As I move to the second location, a behind-the-scenes area of the exhibit, things get tougher, and Proto Man’s other abilities become a factor. While he doesn’t have the range of his blue brother, Proto Man has a powerful shield at his disposal. This can be thrown like a looping boomerang, Captain America-style. Similar to prior playable appearances, he lifts his shield when he jumps. That move saved my life quite a few times, as I jumped over several pits of instant death while birds dropped balls that exploded into a barrage of rockets that would have knocked me away from the platforms had I not blocked the shots.

You don’t get to copy powers from fallen Robot Masters the way Mega Man does. Instead, as best I can tell, the Proto Shield gets new functions or abilities. For this demo, I had two attacks unlocked, a leaping uppercut, and horizontal dive attack. Both were useful in fights (especially the uppercut against the boss of the second area, a knockoff of Astro Man from Mega Man 8), and had some convenient other uses as well. At one point I spied a Bolt in the upper right corner of my screen, too far to jump, but was able to snag it after leaping into one of those horizontal dives. Seems like another series staple, backtracking once you’ve unlocked useful areas to grab all the secrets, is back once again.

It’s nighttime in the final area, as large shapes formed by the fireworks now light up the sky. The going is noticeably tougher here. There are a lot of enemies, a lot of pits, and quite a few platforming sections that put both together, with little margin for error. As you reach the end of each screen, it scrolls over, in classic Mega Man style, and every few screens drops a checkpoint. Gone is the era of limited lives, but you can restart at the most recent checkpoint as much as you need, which seems like a decent compromise to give us old-school Mega Man fans a chance to flex our gameplay muscles without scaring away new players. One particularly tough section has me jumping across a series of ascending fireworks, using them as platforms before they explode, and requires carefully timing my shots as I clear out the enemies blocking my path in the air. That’s an area where the large coverage area of Proto Man’s charged shot is advantageous over the relatively smaller hitbox of Mega Man’s charged buster shot.

When I finally have my showdown with Twinkle Girl, it takes me a few tries to figure out her attacks and how to avoid them. Solving that combat puzzle with Proto Man, with his limited range in mind, forces some strategic rethinking compared to Mega Man. You’ve got to stay tight to land attacks, but not so close that you get hit. He has a narrow window to operate in, which makes for an interesting challenge as I clash with the Robot Master.

One thing that stood out to me in this fight, and throughout the demo, was the visible damage on my character, as well as on some enemies. As you, the other bots, and the boss lose health, a visibly scuffed, beaten up look appears. It’s a small touch, but one I don’t recall seeing before, and a cool little attention to detail.

As my fight with Twinkle Girl nears, she kicks things up a notch, entering a powered-up state, and firing off a series of fireworks blasts before crashing to the ground in an eruption of fire. Not one to be outdone, I activate Proto-Man’s override mode, with a quick, flashy cutscene leading to my own souped-up state. This boost is temporary, and leaves you with diminished offensive capabilities for a brief time after it runs out, so I press the attack. Just as my time is about to run out, I fire a massive charged attack from point-blank range, draining the last of Twinkle Girl’s health as my charred, slightly smoking Proto Man claims victory, in a dramatic finish.

Proto Man offers a distinctly different challenge than Mega Man. Not necessarily harder, just different. It’s worth noting that you won’t be switching back and forth between the two; at the start of your playthrough you’ll select which character to control for the entire run, offering some potential replayability to see the game both ways. I’m particularly curious about the various chips that can be unlocked, how those will affect gameplay, and what sort of moveset a fully upgraded Proto Man will have at his disposal. For that, I’ll have to wait for Mega Man: Dual Override’s launch, scheduled for Spring 2027.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

articles.title: Helldivers Movie Eyes Reacher's Alan Ritchson as Its Star
articles.summary: Reacher star Alan Ritchson is reportedly in talks to star in PlayStation's upcoming Helldivers movie.
articles.body:
Reacher star Alan Ritchson is reportedly in talks to star in PlayStation's upcoming Helldivers movie.

As reported by Deadline , the feature film adaptation of Arrowhead Game Studios' brutal multiplayer hit is zeroing in on a new lead after Aquaman actor Jason Momoa exited the project earlier this year. Ritchson is only said to be in talks for the unnamed Helldivers role so far, but Sony and director Justin Lin will want to move fast if they still want to hit their video game-to-movie adaptation's November 2027 drop date.

Ritchson has emerged as one of the more memorable action faces in the last decade. Although he's best known as the face of Prime Video's Reacher series, he's also shown up in Supergirl, Titans, and Fast X. Most recently, viewers may recognize him from his work in Netflix's War Machine or in this month's Owen Wilson movie, Runner.

Plot details for the Helldivers movie remain tightly under wraps as the crew tries to pin Ritchson behind the scenes. Sony announced plans to bring the battle for Super Earth to the big screen back in January 2025, and although things seemed to be progressing smoothly enough since, a few snags have kept it from landing.

For example, Lin, the director behind some The Fast and the Furious movies, boarded Helldivers in December of last year. Momoa then followed as Sony nailed down a release date in February of this year.

As much sense as it would make to see Momoa buzzing through Terminids and Automatons in the name of liberty, the DC and Game of Thrones star was said to have bailed on Helldivers in June. Why he departed the movie still remains unclear, though fans probably aren't too beaten up over the idea now that Ritchson could be the one to suit up.

Helldivers is still careening toward its November 10, 2027, theatrical release date. While Sony and Ritchson hammer out the details, you can read about how Arrowhead is involved in the production and what its CEO had to say to the director .
